cards.front: public record substrate not accusation product
cards.back: The cube exists to make public accountability records preservable, normalizable, contestable, and useful before it exists to accuse any person.
cards.why_it_matters: A source-bound substrate can support journalism, defense work, research, oversight, families, and community memory without collapsing uncertainty into accusation.

cards.back: The mature cube should make it difficult for officers with serious, source-supported histories to disappear through jurisdictional fragmentation and reappear unobserved elsewhere.
cards.why_it_matters: The seed identifies wandering officers as the most important consequence of fragmented public records.

cards.back: The archive may remember more than it displays, but every public claim must be earned by source custody, bounded wording, claim state, freshness, privacy review, and rollback path.
cards.why_it_matters: The project is legally and morally fragile if it turns partial records into unqualified banners.

cards.back: The cube must be able to represent individual conduct, institutional patterns, policies, contracts, budgets, settlements, supervision, and reform timelines without letting any one layer erase the others.
cards.why_it_matters: A pure officer database feeds the bad-apple frame; a pure institution database can hide repeat individuals.

cards.back: The cube must protect civilians, witnesses, families, minors, survivors, vulnerable communities, and people in crisis even when source records are public.
cards.why_it_matters: Accountability records often contain the names and trauma of people who never consented to becoming data infrastructure.

cards.front: due process is an accountability requirement
cards.back: Allegation, investigation, finding, settlement, reversal, exoneration, acquittal, decertification, reinstatement, and correction must remain distinct.
cards.why_it_matters: The cube should be trustworthy enough to help accountability precisely because it refuses careless collapse.

cards.back: The cube should expose the structure of missing, sealed, destroyed, denied, stale, paywalled, inaccessible, or ambiguous records without pretending that missing means absent.
cards.why_it_matters: Fragmentation itself is one of the accountability facts the project must make legible.

cards.front: serve many civic users without becoming the police tool
cards.back: The cube should support journalists, public defenders, civil-rights litigators, researchers, oversight bodies, families, community organizers, legislators, and monitors while resisting use as police intelligence against civilians.
cards.why_it_matters: The seed names broad civic audiences, but access and presentation choices decide whether the infrastructure helps accountability or surveillance.

cards.back: The cube must preserve local legal vocabulary, agency structures, union contracts, disclosure regimes, and record quirks while normalizing enough to compare across jurisdictions.
cards.why_it_matters: A national corpus becomes false if it erases local meaning; a purely local archive cannot reveal mobility or cross-jurisdiction patterns.

cards.front: corrections and rollback are core not afterthoughts
cards.back: The cube should treat corrections, defeaters, source withdrawal, appeals, stale status, mismerges, and public challenges as ordinary lifecycle events.
cards.why_it_matters: Long-lived accountability infrastructure must expect change and contestation rather than pretending archival entries are static.

cards.back: Future sessions should be allowed to imagine broad products, new pilots, international extensions, and radical civic interfaces, then gate them carefully rather than refusing to dream.
cards.why_it_matters: The project can die by recklessness or by overconstraint; foundation work should protect ambition as well as protect people.

cards.front: the archive should make democracy less forgetful
cards.back: At scale, the cube should turn scattered, perishable, local accountability records into durable democratic memory that communities and institutions can use to act.
cards.why_it_matters: The seed frames the corpus as infrastructure: a shared spine for downstream accountability projects rather than a replacement for them.
